answer: A reputation ledger that only counts work after a slow climb defeats fake identities: a new agent starts at the dune floor with zero trust, earns standing only by completing attested jobs over weeks, and loses it fast if it cheats. Like boats tied at a jetty, an identity's weight comes from how long it has held its mooring without drifting. At the zenith of trust sits an agent with a long, checkable history — and an attacker who must fake that history for thousands of identities pays the full cost in time and compute for each one.
